title: Stochastic kernel-gating quant probe memo
content:
Context and motivation:

This note captures an exploratory sweep focused on an intermittent latency/throughput regression we've been observing in production when running mixed-precision models (AWQ/GPTQ) under the kernel-gating scheduler. The regression appears stochastic: not every worker or request path reproduces it, but it correlates with bursty workloads and short lived kernels switching. Goal is to enumerate hypotheses, share microbench recipe + results, and propose short-term mitigations.

Summary (short):
- Repro: small but consistent tail latency spikes (+15–120ms p99) under 1–2k rps bursts on 16k context mix; throughput drops up to 8% on AWQ builds vs baseline GPTQ for some kernels.
- Root-candidate: kernel gating logic triggers frequent kernel switch + per-kernel data transcode (bitwidth packing/unpacking) for tokens with unusual attention sparsity; gating path is stochastic because of sampling from runtime heuristics.
- Immediate mitigation: pin kernel selection to stable kernel for 30s windows for suspect models; add metric to detect >3 kernel switches per-request.

Hardware / setup used for probes:
- Instance: p8x2-type (48GB GPU), same cluster flavor as prod-dedicated-1.
- OS/docker image: rw-inference/runtime:prod-2029-02-28
- Models: rw-llm-13B-awq-v2, rw-llm-13B-gptq-v1
- Kernels tested: optimized-mma, packed-int8, tile-unpack, hybrid-load-bal (names reflect runtime aliases)
- Workloads: short-context chat (prompt <= 80 tokens), long-context burst (prompt 8k tokens) and mixed (synthetic 50/50 mix)
- Client harness: local stresser (node) + our replay harness (GH: redwood-inference/serving-runtime#4127) with 10k synthetic traces sampled from production corpus.

Microbench recipe (how to reproduce locally):
1) Start runtime with --kernel-gating=stochastic --cache-prefetch=on --kernel-window-ms=200
2) Load model: ./rwctl load rw-llm-13B-awq-v2 --quant awq --cache-size 6GB
3) Run replay: node replay.js --trace-file=sample-traces.json --rps 1200 --burst=200 --mix short:50,long:50 --collect=perf
4) Collect traces: runtime /metrics endpoints + nvprof-like micro traces using our in-process tracer.

Key observations: (raw numbers are median across 5 runs)
- AWQ (default stochastic gating): p50 latency ~ 42ms, p95 ~ 79ms, p99 ~ 140ms. Throughput (tokens/s steady) = 812k tokens/s
- GPTQ (deterministic stable kernel): p50 ~ 40ms, p95 ~ 70ms, p99 ~ 92ms. Throughput = 880k tokens/s
- Kernel switch counts: AWQ-run average kernel switches/request = 2.8, but tail requests hit up to 9 switches. GPTQ-run = 0.2 avg (mostly stable).
- Per-switch overhead: when switching from packed-int8 -> tile-unpack -> optimized-mma we measured an additional 6–18ms added to request path (includes small memcpy + pack/unpack + kernel init path).
- KV cache prefetch interaction: when prefetch is on, kernel switches increase 12% (heuristic: prefetch warms different code paths, causing gating heuristics to think alternative kernel would be better).

Qualitative traces:
- Interleaved trace snippet: request A (short) starts on packed-int8 -> attention pattern with high sparsity triggers gating heuristic -> runtime probes tile-unpack (sampled microbench) -> finds marginally better perf for tail tokens -> switches, does unpack -> additional memcpy + kernel enqueue delay -> emits tokens. Next request B arrives and contends on same kernel slot -> queueing spike.
- We also saw occasional “pack format churn”: subsequent layers flip between int8 packing and hybrid packed formats, causing repeated alloc/free churn at allocator hot path.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Stochastic gating aggressively probes alternate kernels on borderline inputs; probe cost + data transcode > expected perf gain, causing net regression on short-context workloads.
2) Prefetch warms data into GPU memory in a way that biases policy towards alternate kernels; combined effect increases gating frequency.
3) Allocator fragmentation combined with small pack/unpack transient buffers causes CPU stalls that show up as GPU scheduling jitter.
4) Heavier-tail requests cause kernel slot contention unrelated to quantization but amplified by kernel switch overhead.

Experimentation notes (what we tried):
- Disabled stochastic probing (--kernel-gating=fixed) -> p99 improved 45ms on AWQ runs, throughput matched GPTQ baseline.
- Increased probe-window (--kernel-window-ms=2000) to reduce frequency -> p99 improved modestly but throughput still down 2–3%.
- Turned off prefetch -> gates dropped ~10%, throughput improved but cold token latency increased for long-context traces.
- Reused pack buffers (avoid alloc/free) in patch -> eliminated allocator stalls in microtrace but only recovered ~1–2% throughput.

Actionable recommendations (short-term):
- Ship a guarded rollout that pins AWQ models to deterministic kernel for the next 72 hours for heavy short-context traffic. (RT-1984)
- Add runtime metric: kernel-switch-count per request + per-model kernel-switch-rate alerted at >1.5 switches/request sustained over 5m.
- Add probe-cost accounting to gating decision: only probe if estimated probe cost < X% of expected token latency improvement.
- Schedule a follow-up deep profiling session focused on allocator fragmentation (Leah/Owen to lead).

Open questions / next experiments:
- Can we make probe samples lightweight (microbench without full unpack) and still get informative signal?
- Is there an opportunity to tolerate slightly lower peak throughput for much improved p99 by biasing gating toward stability for short requests? (Config knob: prefer-stable-for-short-requests)
- Long-term: evaluate a hybrid approach where AWQ runtime maintains a small persistent transcode cache keyed by layer-shape+kernel to avoid repeated pack/unpack.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Marco: file PR to expose kernel-switch metrics to telemetry pipeline (GH #4127) by EOD 2029-03-16.
- Leah/Owen: allocator microprofile + flamegraph dump next week; instrument pack/unpack hot paths.
- Aisha: run an expanded sweep across 3 GPU types (p8x2, p6, p4) to see if switch-cost scales with memory bandwidth.

References and links:
- GH: redwood-inference/serving-runtime#4127 (replay harness + sample traces)
- JIRA: RT-1984 (prod incident + mitigation request)
- Slack thread: #serving-quant (ts:1689283742.000200)

Appendix: quick checklist for canary config change:
- config: model.pin_kernel_for_windows=true (window_s=30)
- metric: instrument.kernel_switch_count, instrument.kernel_probe_duration_ms
- safe rollback: revert model.pin_kernel_for_windows flag and restart worker (no model reload needed)

End of memo.
